Package common.core.fsm

Class FSMSubsystemBase<S extends Enum<S>>

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
common.core.fsm.FSMSubsystemBase<S>
Type Parameters:
S - The enum listing this subsystem's states
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
public abstract class FSMSubsystemBase<S extends Enum<S>> extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
A subsystem that is always in one of a fixed list of states, like NEUTRAL, INTAKE or SHOOT, and only moves between them along the transitions you allow.

To make one:

  1. List the states in an enum.
  2. Extend this class and build its mechanisms in the constructor.
  3. In registerTransitions(), add a Transition for every move between states that's allowed, with the command that does it.

 public class Intake extends FSMSubsystemBase<IntakeStates> {
     private static final TransitionMap<IntakeStates> transitionMap = new TransitionMap<>(IntakeStates.class);

     public Intake() {
         super(IntakeStates.class, transitionMap, IntakeStates.NEUTRAL);
         roller = new RollerMechanism(...);
         addMechanisms(roller);
     }

     public void registerTransitions() {
         // Any state can go to any other, running the roller at that state's power
         transitionMap.addCommutativeTransition(List.of(IntakeStates.values()),
             state -> roller.runCommand(state.getPower()));
     }
 }

Then intake.setState(IntakeStates.INTAKE) runs the transition's command. Asking for a move that isn't in the map does nothing and logs a warning, which keeps a subsystem from doing something unplanned, like extending an arm through the robot.

The current state is logged to NetworkTables under StateMachines/<name> whenever it changes, so you can follow it in AdvantageScope or a log file.

    • initShuffleboard

      public void initShuffleboard()
      Adds a Shuffleboard tab with the current and previous state, whether the last request was allowed, and a light for every state that's on when the subsystem is in it.

    • overrideState

      public void overrideState(S nextState)
      Changes the state without running any transition or checking it's allowed. Use it to correct the state after something outside the state machine moved the mechanisms, not to move them yourself.

    • setState

      public void setState(S nextState)
      Moves to nextState by running the transition registered for it, if there is one.
      • If the move isn't allowed, nothing changes and a warning is logged.
      • If a transition is still running, it's cancelled and the new one starts.
      • The state changes as soon as the transition starts, not when its command finishes. Use isTransitioning() to check whether it's still moving.

      The first call registers the transitions, if registerTransitions() hasn't filled the map yet.
